newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator calls for start on new arms treaty.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator calls for start on new arms treaty.

text.p: A key Republican senator called on Wednesday for stepped-up U.S. pressure on Russia to ratify a nuclear weapons reduction treaty and for work to begin on a follow-up pact.
Sen. Richard Lugar, an Indiana Republican, said delay in implementing the START-2 treaty as many Russian officials were seeking would be costly to both countries.
Lugar, a senior member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, this month accompanied Defence Secretary William Perry on a trip to Russia for talks with Russian leaders.
He told a news conference Washington was in danger of missing a window of opportunity by putting relations with Russia and Russian denuclearization on the back burner.

"The United States leadership ought to focus its attention on developments in Russia each day, not with periodic fits of alarm such as those observed in the press and public discussion of the last two weeks," he said.

Lugar, who is author with Georgia Democrat Sam Nunn of a law under which the United States gives aid to Russia to destroy its missiles, said Washington should press Moscow to ratify the START-2 treaty without renegotiation or delay.

If the treaty was delayed for five years as argued by many Russian officials, the United States would be faced with a $4 billion bill just to maintain weapons it wished to destroy, Lugar said. The Russians would face a similar expense.
He said Washington should provide more denuclearization aid under the Nunn-Lugar law, reducing chances that nuclear weapons technology would fall into the wrong hands.

Lugar said also that the United States should outline a framework for a potential START-3 treaty and begin negotiations on further weapons reductions as soon as START-2 was ratified. Lowering the ceiling on warheads would mean Russia would not have to build the full complement of single-warhead missiles allowed under the present treaty, he said.
